title: The played bed over a whole 500,000-frame session
question: Which bed is still alive at the end of a session?
context_md:
This is the answer to your question on the last card -- *"it is about to get destroyed or is it coming back?"* -- run out to the end instead of stopping at 60,000 frames.

The same bed and the same seed as that card (played_bed, seed 3), from the first frame to frame 500,000. 251 captures, one every 2,000 world frames, about ten seconds a loop, so the whole session plays as a time-lapse. The frame counter is in the top-left corner. Both arms are one scenario and one seed; the only thing between them is what a bite does to a seed, and whether a leaf on a living plant is worth eating.

**Watch the middle of the loop.** Both beds thin out badly around 100,000-250,000 frames while the colony is at its biggest. The question is what happens after that.

The counters below are the paired 500,000-frame census on this same bed and seed. They are given as a pair rather than split between the two panes, so the panes stay judged by eye:

| at frame 500,000 | |
|---|---|
| plants standing | **2 against 114** |
| seed bank | **0 against 402** |
| ants | 0 against 0 -- both colonies are gone by the end |
| columns with no plant, away from the nest | **254 of 383 against 11 of 383** |
| seed larder | 0.7 kJ against 47.8 kJ |
| leaf larder | 273.5 kJ at 20,000 frames falling to 3.4 kJ, against 0.0 the whole way -- a live leaf is deliberately not food any more |
| seeds carried home over the session | 0 against 2,778 |
| plants grown from a carried seed | 0 against 156 |

items.label: main -- a bitten seed is destroyed, and a live leaf is a full meal
